<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Avimārakam is considered to be a fairy tale and draws inspiration from Bṛhatkathā. The story is said to be original and is a semi-social drama. It is a simple love story with the initial separation, followed by pining and the eventual happy reunion. The play receives its title from the name of the hero who is so named on account of being the killer (Māraka) of a demon in the form of a sheep (Avi)</div></div></div>

Water can only be obtained from the earth by digging; consequently, nothing is impossible for courageous persons who choose the proper path and always succeed. 3. यतने ्ृ रे यदद न ससधयपर ्ोऽत्र दोषः । ्ो ्व् न ससधयपर ्म्मेपर ्रोपर ््यगा्म् ॥ यतननः शुभनः िुरुषर् भ्वरीह नॄण््म् । दन्वं प्व््न्मनुरच्छपर ््यगाससद्धः ॥          \[अप्व्म्र््म् – ३.१२\] yatne kṛte yadi na sidhyati ko'tra doṣaḥ | ko vā na sidhyati mameti karoti kāryam || yatnaiḥ śubhaiḥ puruṣatā bhavatīha nṝṇām | daivaṃ vidhānamanugacchati kāryasiddhiḥ ||</div></div></div>
